summary: Long sessions are neither free speed nor inevitable decay; measurement can still mislead if task mix and repair attribution are weak.

points.text: Fresh sessions provide isolation and a clean statement of intent. For high-risk, unrelated or policy-sensitive work, that boundary may be worth more than any orientation saving.

Repair density can rise simply because later tasks are harder. Compare similar task classes, models and validation regimes, and report uncertainty instead of declaring session age causal from a raw correlation.
A repair is often discovered after the session ends. TE needs a stable session identifier and delayed linkage from review findings or reopened tasks back to the session-age bucket that produced them.
Compact checkpoints themselves cost time and can discard useful tacit context. Count checkpoint and reorientation overhead when evaluating a restart policy.
